recommended_approach.pattern: UIHostingController-based incremental integration with single-direction state ownership and UIKit-owned navigation
best_practices: Use UIHostingController to embed SwiftUI views in existing UIKit navigation stacks — zero navigation rewrite, push SwiftUI screens onto UINavigationController via hosting controller, remove NavigationStack from embedded views to avoid double navigation bars

Pick leaf screens first — start with low-traffic, low-complexity screens (settings, static detail, simple forms) that have no child view controllers; avoid migrating the most-trafficked screen first to contain regression blast radius
Define a feature boundary contract before migrating — UIKit owns navigation and lifecycle, SwiftUI owns rendering and local state, ViewModels coordinate both sides without UI framework imports

Use @Observable (Observation framework) over ObservableObject + @Published for iOS 18+; UIKit automatic observation tracking (iOS 18+) re-renders views when observable properties change without manual invalidation
Keep ViewModels UI-framework-agnostic — no UIColor, UIImage, or UIKit imports in ViewModel layer; same ViewModel powers both UIKit and SwiftUI versions, enabling test reuse across migrations

Add snapshot tests (swift-snapshot-testing by Point-Free) as the primary regression safety net — record golden images on first migration, diff every subsequent run; commit reference images to source control for visual regression detection in CI
Use .task instead of .onAppear for one-time async operations — .onAppear can fire multiple times during SwiftUI view lifecycle re-renders, causing duplicate API calls
Enable UIHostingController.sizingOptions = [.intrinsicContentSize] on iOS 16+ when embedding SwiftUI sections within UIKit screens via Auto Layout constraints
Pass explicit dismiss/pop callbacks to hosted SwiftUI views — @Environment(\.dismiss) does not work for UIHostingController pushed by UIKit; use closures or a NavigationBridge object
Apply environment modifiers to the root view before passing it to UIHostingController — the hosting controller does not support adding environment values after creation without reassigning rootView
Use UIHostingConfiguration for SwiftUI content inside UICollectionViewCell and UITableViewCell — lightweight, preferred over managing child hosting controllers for cell-level migrations

Run snapshot/visual baseline checks on high-traffic screens and unit tests on feature logic parity; define rollback criteria before each release (e.g., crash rate rises above baseline by X% → rollback within one release window)
Migrate feature-by-feature, not file-by-file — a feature migration unit must include view, interactions, analytics events, error states, and accessibility checks
Keep a migration scorecard each sprint tracking: screens migrated, defects introduced, regression incidents, net delivery speed impact
regression_risks: Double navigation bars — SwiftUI NavigationStack inside UIHostingController pushed onto UINavigationController creates two navigation bars
@Environment(\.dismiss) silent failure — no crash, but dismissal simply does not work when SwiftUI view is pushed via UIHostingController from UIKit navigation stack
ViewModel recreated repeatedly — using @ObservedObject instead of @StateObject on views that create their own ViewModel causes state loss on every SwiftUI re-render
Missing environment values crash — SwiftUI view expects @Environment object not provided at UIHostingController creation causes runtime crash
API calls firing multiple times — using .onAppear for data loading instead of .task causes duplicate network requests during SwiftUI view lifecycle re-renders
Hosted view zero-size in Auto Layout — UIHostingController without .intrinsicContentSize sizing option on iOS 16+ causes container collapse
Safe area propagation failure — tab bar insets or custom safe areas from UIKit not respected by hosted SwiftUI view content
State ownership confusion — shared state mutated from both UIKit and SwiftUI sides creates unpredictable UI state
Performance regression in lists — SwiftUI recreates views eagerly unlike UIKit's cell reuse; LazyVStack/LazyHGrid mitigate but need profiling for 10,000+ item lists
Analytics and experiment parity gaps — UIKit navigation tracking hooks may not fire when navigation is handled through SwiftUI NavigationStack or sheet modifiers
Lifecycle mismatch — SwiftUI state-driven lifecycle may call side effects at unexpected times compared to UIKit's predictable viewWillAppear/viewDidAppear sequence
mitigation_strategies: Keep navigation owned by UIKit — do not add NavigationStack inside SwiftUI views embedded in UINavigationController; use UIHostingController as the bridge and pass explicit callbacks for push/pop/dismiss
Use @StateObject for ViewModel ownership on views that create their own model; use @ObservedObject only when the ViewModel is injected from a parent that already owns it
Use .task { } modifier for async data loading — it automatically cancels when the view disappears and only fires once per view identity, unlike .onAppear which can fire multiple times

Pre-set all environment values on root view before passing to UIHostingController — e.g., .environmentObject(MyModel()).environment(\.managedObjectContext, context) — and wrap in a container view if values need to change after creation
Always set hostingVC.view.backgroundColor = .clear when embedding SwiftUI over existing UIKit content to avoid opaque white background covering the parent's appearance
Store UIHostingController in a property — if only held as a child view controller, removing from parent deallocates it and the SwiftUI view disappears
Establish explicit rollback criteria before each migration release: define crash rate and performance thresholds that trigger automatic rollback within one release window
Add snapshot tests for every migrated screen state (loading, populated, empty, error) with swift-snapshot-testing; commit golden images to source control and use Git LFS for snapshot files
Use UIHostingConfiguration for table/collection view cells instead of managing child hosting controllers — lighter weight and handles reuse correctly
Instrument route transitions for observability — ensure analytics events fire equivalently for both UIKit and SwiftUI navigation paths during migration
Run a migration scorecard each sprint: track screens migrated, defects introduced, regression incidents, and net delivery speed impact to validate the migration strategy is improving outcomes

Phase migration rollout: days 1-15 baseline metrics + architecture standards, days 16-30 bridge layer + routing rules, days 31-50 low-risk screens + analytics parity, days 51-70 medium-complexity flows + snapshot checks + canary releases
